title: Zelenskyy Replaces Ukraine's Military Chief After Days of Street Protests
excerpt: Mykhailo Drapatyi, a 43-year-old combat veteran who rose from tank lieutenant to joint forces commander, becomes Ukraine's youngest-ever commander-in-chief.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Zelenskyy replaced military chief Syrskyi with 43-year-old Mykhailo Drapatyi amid public protests.
  • Drapatyi is Ukraine's youngest commander-in-chief, known for his combat experience and leadership.
  • Protests erupted after the dismissal of popular Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, demanding accountability.
  • The Kremlin dismissed the leadership change, predicting no impact on the front lines.
Leadership Shake-Up in Ukraine
›Age: 43 Mykhailo Drapatyi appointed as commander-in-chief.
›Youngest commander-in-chief in Ukraine's history Drapatyi's rise from tank lieutenant to top commander.
›Protests in multiple cities: Kyiv, Odesa Public protests followed the dismissal of Defence Minister Fedorov.
›Dismissed after public outcry Syrskyi served as commander-in-chief since February 2024.
  • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi and replaced him with 43-year-old Mykhailo Drapatyi, the youngest person to hold the position.
  • The shake-up followed days of widespread street protests triggered by the earlier firing of popular Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
  • Drapatyi, a decorated tank officer famous for a 2014 barricade-crashing incident in Mariupol, is seen as representing a newer generation of Ukrainian military leaders.
  • The Kremlin dismissed the reshuffle, with spokesperson Dmitry Peskov calling Kyiv's leadership "shaking" and predicting no change on the front lines.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday dismissed his top military commander, General Oleksandr Syrskyi, and named Major General Mykhailo Drapatyi as the country's new commander-in-chief — the most significant shake-up of Ukraine's military leadership since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022.

The decision came after days of protests across Ukrainian cities, driven by public anger over Zelenskyy's earlier removal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a 35-year-old former tech minister who had become widely popular for championing drone warfare and technology-first military strategy.

From Protests to Palace Reshuffle

Fedorov's dismissal last week triggered an unusually open display of public discontent in wartime Ukraine. Thousands took to the streets in Kyiv, Odesa, and other cities, demanding accountability from the country's civilian and military leadership. The protests were notable both for their scale and for the speed with which they forced a response from the presidential office.

On Monday, Zelenskyy's chief of staff issued a statement acknowledging that "the position of society has been heard." Within hours, Syrskyi — who had served as commander-in-chief since February 2024 — was relieved of his duties.

"This is a new wind and a new hope in the struggle of free people for freedom and justice," former Defence Minister Fedorov wrote on Telegram, congratulating Drapatyi on his appointment.

In announcing the change, Zelenskyy thanked Syrskyi for his role in defending Kyiv in the early days of the invasion and leading multiple offensive operations. "We share the same wish, which is victory over the enemy," he said.

Who Is Mykhailo Drapatyi

Drapatyi, 43, represents a generation of Ukrainian officers whose entire senior careers have been forged in combat against Russian forces. Born in western Ukraine and educated at a military school in Kharkiv, he rose from a tank lieutenant to become one of the country's most respected field commanders.

He first gained national attention in 2014, during the early days of Russia's intervention in eastern Ukraine, when a video surfaced of him driving an armoured infantry fighting vehicle through a separatist barricade in Mariupol. The footage went viral and established his reputation as a decisive, front-line commander.

After Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, Drapatyi's forces halted a Russian advance on Kryvyi Rih — Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine — and helped liberate several settlements in the Kherson and Dnipropetrovsk regions. He was appointed commander of the Ukrainian Land Forces in 2024 and elevated to commander of the Joint Forces in 2025.

Upon his appointment, Drapatyi vowed to work "responsibly, with focus and with respect" for Ukraine's troops. He thanked Syrskyi, noting: "I grew up in its ranks."

Syrskyi's Controversial Tenure

Syrskyi, 60, was born in Russia's Vladimir region and trained at a Moscow military school — a biography that drew criticism from some Ukrainian nationalists throughout his tenure. He was credited with the successful defence of Kyiv in 2022 and the Kharkiv counteroffensive later that year, but his leadership style attracted persistent controversy.

Critics gave him the nickname "the Butcher" for his willingness to hold positions at heavy human cost, particularly during the prolonged defence of Bakhmut. In a rare public statement on Monday, Syrskyi defended his record on drone warfare, writing that he could not "switch a million-people army to drones in two months" and calling such expectations "a reckless venture."

Zelenskyy also appointed a new Chief of the General Staff, Major General Ihor Skybyuk, completing a near-total overhaul of Ukraine's top military leadership.

Kremlin Response

The Kremlin was characteristically dismissive. Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Wednesday that he did not expect the reshuffle to "lead to any changes on the front lines," adding that "the Kyiv regime is shaking — this is obvious." Western analysts offered a more measured assessment, noting that Drapatyi's combat experience and relative youth could bring operational flexibility to a military that has been grinding through attritional warfare for more than four years.

The reshuffle leaves Zelenskyy with a military leadership team that is demonstrably younger and more closely aligned with the technology-driven warfare strategy that Fedorov championed. Whether that translates into battlefield results will be tested in the coming months, as Ukraine continues to fight a war that shows no signs of ending.
